thread.subject: [TITAD] @miabhuta PR Collab: K-Salon Scalp Detox at Home 🤎

deliverables: Post 1 dedicated TikTok video featuring TITAD Advanced Scalp Detox Clarifying Shampoo
Upload within 1 week of receiving campaign guideline email
Share video URL & Spark Ads Code by given deadline

factors.exclusivity: No exclusivity mentioned, which is favorable. However, commercial rights usage at below-floor rates represents the primary term concern.
factors.brandRelevance: Haircare shampoo has minimal connection to soccer performance or athlete lifestyle content. The brand lacks athletic market presence and offers limited strategic value for growing your soccer-focused following.
factors.rateComparison: The $300 commercial rights option in your counter-proposal is 71% below your $1,044 floor. Even with products, this undervalues your rates. Your product-only option is appropriately priced at $0 but must explicitly exclude all commercial rights.
factors.deliverableScope: Single TikTok video is reasonable, but the Spark Ads Code requirement indicates commercial usage rights that should command your full floor rate, not a discounted $300.

reasons: Commercial rights undervalued: $300 option is 71% below your $1,044 floor, even with products included
Weak brand alignment: haircare shampoo doesn't resonate with soccer performance or build athletic credibility
Predatory initial offer: brand sought commercial rights for product-only, indicating lowball negotiation tactics
Minimal growth potential: unlikely to drive meaningful follower growth or build relevant brand capital
redFlags: Brand's initial product-only offer demanded commercial rights (Spark Ads Code), a common exploitative practice
Negotiation structure suggests brand is seeking maximum rights for minimum compensation
draft_points: I need to clarify my previous counter-proposal
My floor rate for any commercial rights usage is $1,044
I cannot grant Spark Ads Code usage for $300
Product-only must mean zero commercial rights

brandAnalysis.brandSummary: TITAD is an emerging haircare brand offering scalp detox shampoo. The brand lacks athletic market presence and offers limited strategic overlap with soccer performance content. While personal care is universal, this category doesn't build athletic credibility or naturally engage your soccer audience.

score.recommendation_agent: You should not have offered commercial rights for $300. Immediately clarify to the brand that the $300 option is withdrawn. Present only two viable paths: (1) Product-only with zero commercial rights, no Spark Ads Code, or (2) $1,044+ cash for full commercial rights plus products. The haircare category offers weak strategic fit, so path (1) is only acceptable if you genuinely want the product. Do not grant commercial usage below your floor. If they push back on the $300 option you floated, politely retract it and reference your established rates. This deal lacks the brand alignment to justify any rate flexibility.

brand.name: TITAD
brand.description: Personal Care & Beauty. TITAD is a clean lifestyle brand launched in 2021, focused on personal care products with an emphasis on veganism and sustainability. The company's core philosophy centers on providing natural, clean ingredient products that can be used confidently by the entire family, including specialized items for children. Their product range includes hair treatments, oral care, body care, and other personal care items, sold through various platforms in South Korea and internationally.
brand.audience_summary: Health and wellness-conscious consumers seeking clean, vegan, and sustainable lifestyle products for themselves and their families, with particular appeal to families with children due to their junior product lines.
